To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pathophysiological mechanisms of IBS are complex, including brain‐gut interaction, genetic predisposition, and environmental factors, and these mechanisms are not fully understood yet.
the pathogenesis of IBS is not only related to genetic factors but also to environmental factors, and brain‐ gut interactions are important to understand the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of IBS.
IBS is a disorder that relates to gene x environment interactions and brain‐guts interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic predisposition and the influence of environment on IBS.
the pathophysiological mechanisms of functional gastrointestinal diseases (FGID), especially irritable bowel syndrome, and with the development of novel therapeutic strategies for FGID.
understanding the role of gene x environment interactions in irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathogenesis of IBS is a result of the interaction between genetic predisposition, environmental factors, and brain‐ gut interactions.
IBS may develop by gene‐environment interactions, which may be modulated by brain‐gut interaction, and that the brain may be affected by gut microbiota.
the gene‐brain‐gut interaction is the most important concept in the pathogenesis of IBS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene x environment interaction and brain‐gust interactions are important in IBS pathogenesis.
the brain‐gut axis plays an important role in IBS development and the brain‐gastrointestinal axis is an important target for the treatment of IBS.
the brain‐gut axis is an important concept in IBS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IBS is a disorder of brain‐gat interactions.
the brain‐gut axis is a complex network of neural, hormonal, and immunologic pathways that can influence gut function and symptoms.
